app.title: Chemometric Workbench (RUO)
app.summary: A person loads a table of samples with numeric features, either an uploaded CSV or generated demo spectra, and chooses the feature columns, a preprocessing method, the number of principal components and a confidence level. They explore the PCA model through scree, score and loading plots, then check every sample against Hotelling's T² and Q-residual limits and download the outlier diagnostics. Next they choose a numeric target and fit a PLS regression with a train/test split and cross-validation. For that model they see error metrics, a component sweep, a ranking of the features with the most influence, applicability-domain checks and uncertainty levels. Last, they export the predictions with in-domain and review-required flags, and they can also save the fitted model.

task.text: Build a PCA and PLS model on multivariate analytical measurements, flag samples that fall outside it, and export predictions that carry applicability-domain, uncertainty and review flags.

data.text: A table of samples with many numeric features, such as absorbance at each wavelength of a spectrum, plus optional metadata columns: an id, a group and a numeric target property.
data.item: one sample: a row holding its spectrum or analytical measurements

stage.text: exploring and modelling multivariate analytical measurements, before an analyst reviews the flagged samples

mechanism.text: Sidebar controls set the data, feature columns, preprocessing, number of components and confidence level, and every tab recomputes when they change. The tabs show the data table, the PCA plots, the T²/Q influence plot with its control limits, and the PLS results: metrics, plots, applicability domain and uncertainty. Each tab ends in a CSV download.

field.text: PCA outlier diagnostics and PLS multivariate calibration in chemometrics

workflow.name: fit a multivariate model, flag samples outside it, and export predictions with review flags

steps.here: The sidebar offers a synthetic NIR-like spectra demo (sample count and seed) or a CSV upload. The person then picks the feature columns and a column to colour points by.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: The person chooses a preprocessing method (mean-center, autoscale, SNV, MSC or Savitzky-Golay), the number of PCA components and the confidence limit, then reads the scree plot, a score plot with selectable axes, and loadings for chosen components.

steps.step: identify the items that break a limit
steps.here: Each sample is plotted as Hotelling's T² against Q-residual, with F-distribution and Jackson-Mudholkar limits, and gets a verdict. Flagged samples are listed with their counts, and the diagnostics download as a CSV.

steps.step: fit a predictive model and check its error
steps.here: The person picks a target column, test fraction, CV folds and number of PLS components. The tab shows test and CV RMSE and R², predicted-vs-actual and residual plots, a CV RMSE component sweep, and a predictions table.

steps.step: judge how far each prediction can be trusted
steps.here: Features are ranked by standardized coefficient, with a top-N slider. Mahalanobis distance and leverage set each sample in or out of domain. Uncertainty from CV residuals gives each sample a LOW, MEDIUM or HIGH level, and a review-required flag is set when a sample is out of domain or HIGH.
Downloads cover the predictions CSV, the fitted model as a PKL, the feature influence CSV, and one consolidated CSV of predictions with domain and uncertainty fields.

distinctive: Outliers are split by kind: high T² means extreme but consistent with the model, high Q means a poor fit to the model, and samples high on both are strong outliers. Both limits are derived statistically at the chosen confidence level.
Spectral preprocessing options (SNV, MSC, Savitzky-Golay derivative) are applied before both PCA and PLS.
Every prediction carries an applicability-domain flag (Mahalanobis distance and leverage limits) and an uncertainty level, which combine into a review-required flag.
A component sweep plots CV RMSE against the number of PLS components so the person can pick model complexity.
The demo data comes with injected T² and Q outliers so the diagnostics have something to find.
